I brought my dog ​​for a superficial ulcer. I was treated by a very professional and kind young doctor.
Congratulations 👏

I would like to express my deepest and sincere gratitude to the entire Gregorio VII Veterinary Clinic for the extraordinary professionalism, kindness, and dedication they demonstrated in caring for my furry little boy. In such delicate times, finding a medical and human team of this caliber is not a given.

A special thank you to each and every professional who accompanied us on this journey:
Marco Bertoli, for his impeccable and timely management of the nighttime emergency room.
Alessandra Lonigro, for the care and dedication she showed during his hospitalization.
Claudia Colucci, Giulia Maggi, and Lavinia Aghilone, for the precision and sensitivity of their examinations.
Olga Marrone, for her expertise, empathy, and closeness.
All the veterinary technicians who cared for him every day with love and constant attention.

A heartfelt thanks also goes to the administrative/reception department, especially to Alessia and her tall, young colleague (whose name, unfortunately, I don't remember), always welcoming and kind.

Finally, I'd like to reflect on costs and quality.
It's true, prices aren't affordable, but it's crucial to remember that unlike us humans, our pets don't have a National Health Service. Maintaining such high quality standards, both in terms of the excellence of our technological equipment and the rigorous selection of our trained veterinarians, comes at an inevitable cost. Expertise is invaluable: I truly hope the clinic continues along this path, investing in quality and, above all, in the training of its staff, because that's exactly what makes the difference for our pets' health.
Excellence in Rome.
Convenient vet with huge parking

The clinic, which was very thorough in caring for my dog, and I must say saved his life, since we presented with type C heart failure, suddenly disappeared on the fourth day of care. After receiving a call at 7:00 in the morning saying that my dog ​​was being discharged, they didn't hear from me again for the rest of the day, until I had to go to the emergency room at 10:00 that evening to find out what had happened to my pet. I discovered that the person in charge of my dog's discharge was a certain Dr. Baio, a cardiologist with whom I never spoke until the moment of arrival at the emergency room, and who had simply forgotten to perform the entire procedure. The dog was discharged two days later in a total state of confusion because he had stayed too long in the hospital without the necessary prescriptions for the medications, which were sold to me at the time by the hospital itself. Even though my dog ​​has a heart condition, I have not received any information from Dr. Baio, who always appears to be responsible for my pet. But she has never been seen and has also forgotten to fill my prescriptions. Therefore, I am unable to refill my medications today. If the aforementioned doctor does not write me the prescription requested since 11:00 this morning. The prescription has not yet been written. In a little while, I will not be able to communicate with the clinic, and tonight my dog ​​has to take a life-saving therapy.

I took my cat to the emergency room and the reception was: "What is he doing here, what does he want?" Then, after my explanations and without looking at the cat, he said either wait until 8 (it was 7) for my colleague to arrive or go somewhere else. Needless to say, I left.
Thank you so much for your feedback! We're happy you had a positive experience.
Good and reasonable
Thanks to all the doctors at the hospital, they are angels for our "children"

Very positive impression.
Competent and friendly medical staff
Thank you so much for your feedback! We're happy you had a positive experience.
Excellent

Guys, I say this with all my heart to anyone reading these reviews wondering whether it's worth bringing their pet to this clinic.
Maybe, like me, you have an emergency but want to be sure of the people you're entrusting your dog/cat to, DO NOT BRING HIM HERE.
They are terrible animals. I've been to veterinary clinics, but I've never felt such little empathy and indifference towards these poor souls.
I took my dog ​​to this clinic last night, SEPTEMBER 20, 2026, because he had blood in his urine. They suspected cystitis and gave him a painkiller and sent him home. The dog started breathing heavily and took about 100 breaths in a minute, which is absolutely NOT NORMAL. He was in terrible pain and couldn't walk, so I decided to take him back. The vet, Paolo Gaglio, responded by saying there was nothing he could do, there was nothing they could do, and he couldn't even admit him.
I hope you're reading this because my dog ​​was admitted to another facility where they actually confirmed he wasn't well.
At this point, I'm wondering how the assessment of a veterinarian (an incompetent one, I might add) can be completely different from the assessment of another who tries to do everything possible and rule out any possibility for the animal's well-being.
You've completely failed in your work, and in the true sense of the word, which isn't about profit, not just that.
You should be ashamed; you have souls on your conscience.
Thank you so much for your feedback! We're happy you had a positive experience.

Terrible experience. After making us wait over two hours for my cat, the doctor was rude and disrespectful. He quoted us around €1,500 for two days of hospitalization. They're not very kind, they're taking advantage of the fact that people love animals. Never again! I could write many more things, but I'll stop here. Bye!
Thank you so much for your feedback! We're happy you had a positive experience.

Terrible experience with the nighttime emergency room at the Policlinico Veterinario Gregorio VII. After dozens of unanswered calls, I showed up with my cat in critical condition. The doctor on duty treated me with extreme rudeness, without even checking the animal's condition, and literally slammed the door in my face. My cat died a few hours later. This behavior I found shameful and totally incompatible with an emergency room service. I do not recommend it.
Peaceful environment and highly skilled professionals. Excellent hospitality.

My experiences at this clinic have been varied and conflicting. I've taken my dog ​​for checkups several times. The neurology and ophthalmology departments have been very good, and they've become a point of reference. In the orthopedics department, however, I had a terrible experience: if I had listened to the orthopedist (considered one of the best, but not always on-site because he comes from out of town), I would have had to spend a lot of money and needlessly operate on my dog's elbows. I say needlessly, because elsewhere my dog ​​was deemed perfectly healthy, with official x-rays confirming the complete absence of elbow dysplasia.

I saved a poodle from certain death because they wanted to put him down. He needs surgery on his hind legs. I had a CT scan and x-ray with measurements done on July 9th. I called every day to get an answer, and I received it after almost two months. I paid €450, but to this day they still haven't given me the paper report. "Maybe they need to invent the typewriter again!" All that aside, I found the experience negative; I wouldn't even give it one star! I'm desperately looking for an orthopedic surgeon who isn't as expensive as these ones. I don't have much money, but I think a little humanity is needed even in these clinics, because not all of us can afford them, and it's not easy to help these poor creatures.

August 20th the cat was sick he hadn't defecated for 4 days.. an adopted cat.. a bit furious to leave the house.. and subject him to medical treatment.. I went to the nearest one in the area.. classic small veterinary practice with few medical instruments.. started by saying you have to bring me an ultrasound and we'll see.. beginning of the illness look for a veterinary laboratory to have me do an ultrasound bring the cat back the next day for treatment.. go to the pharmacy buy medicines spend a lot of money, get infections for 10 days.. worsen his pathology.. so far my experience.. I recommend going directly to the facilities with instruments and staff always available.. today I was at the clinic they solved the problem.. the cat is fine they came to my aid with the costs given everything that had happened to me around small veterinary practices and medicines.. I had spent € 700 specifically worsening the actual diagnosis.. I recommend this clinic they are helpful and humane professionals.. Thank you very much Dr. Francesco
Thank you so much for your feedback! We're happy you had a positive experience.
Thank you so much for your feedback! We're happy you had a positive experience.
Thank you so much for your feedback! We're happy you had a positive experience.

They don't take reservations. You arrive and wait in line, but they're very quick.
The appetizers are delicious; the amatriciana is excellent. The wine is delicious on its own. Fair prices.

I took my two-month-old kitten to the emergency room for herpes virus symptoms (with severe conjunctivitis). The visit was very rushed, and the treatment showed no visible improvement. Within a month,
it was extremely difficult to schedule a follow-up appointment, so I had to change vets. The vet not only treated the kitten within seven days, but also discovered ear mites.
For emergencies, I recommend finding another vet.

I took my cat to the emergency room because she suddenly wouldn't move from the pain in her four legs, and after a three-hour wait, they told me they couldn't see her because they didn't have the equipment (?). I returned the next day, and after a full x-ray, the orthopedic doctor told me there was nothing wrong with her, postponing the issue until blood tests were done. A week later, no one had sent me the tests or prescribed a treatment. Despite reminders, I've never been contacted by a doctor again, and the tests performed were incomplete. We paid €400, and no one was able to tell us she had contracted a virus (as our new vet told us). If you have an emergency, I recommend going elsewhere because they ignore you even if the problem could be fatal.
Very professional and attentive
Thank you for your review! Our team works hard every day to provide the best service possible.
Thank you for sharing your experience and for your trust in us! We work passionately to ensure quality care and attention for all the pets who trust us.
Thank you for your positive feedback! Pet welfare and owner satisfaction are our top priorities.
The Policlinico is welcoming, with competent and reliable staff both in reception and in animal services.
We're so happy to read your review! Our team works passionately to offer the best for every pet. Thank you for sharing your experience!
Good experience, but high prices. There's often a mess at the entrance between the dog and cat areas, which isn't pleasant for cat owners.

Total disgust.
I took the dog to a clinic that was packed because it was a small area. They did an ultrasound and it was clear the dog was in an emergency situation with severe gastric torsion. They told me to bring him here. I took a taxi amidst all this, came here to Gregorio, where it's enormous, and found myself faced with a being I wouldn't even call a "human being." He didn't even examine the dog. He even said Alphavet had sent him three cases last night, when they told me that wasn't true. Furthermore, I hear that "the dog is fine, dancing, and having fun." A dog that had vomited shortly before, was complaining of pain, and was experiencing severe nausea and agitation. But according to him, the dog is fine. He didn't even stabilize my dog ​​with fluids. He refused to provide first aid to a dog at risk of gastric torsion, which could lead to death. Reportable. He didn't even examine him; he sent me away. He also told me that if he feels ill in the next two or three hours, not to come here. Whoever you are who works here and was on duty at around 6:30, you suck not only as a vet, but as a person.

If it had been possible, I would have chosen not to give any stars, as my experience with this facility was so devastating, but unfortunately, at least one is obligatory. I lost my dog ​​after a very expensive hospital stay during which, in my opinion, he didn't receive the full attention he needed from the doctors on duty and the medical staff because, according to them, they feared he would be bitten. I'm speechless! I'm talking about a small 11-year-old poodle with only two teeth left, poor thing! This was the excuse they gave for not cleaning him properly. I found his eyes and face constantly dirty. The surgeon was nonexistent, never seen, impossible to get an update on his health, not even when my dog ​​passed away. Rude doctors. They literally threw my dog, who was only dying, into my arms despite the many requests to at least say goodbye. It was immensely painful. I had asked for one humane gesture from everyone: to call me if his condition worsened, and I was called only after my puppy had passed away. An immense pain, and I was even accused of having "attacked" the person who had broken the news to me over the phone... I won't comment further.
My dog ​​is now gone, and on the death certificate, despite my heartfelt requests, the time of death is not listed, after having paid these people a very high bill.
To me, you are just a money-making machine.
Courteous and attentive. You always hope you don't need them, but this is the place I recommend when you do.

This is another facility that, unfortunately, I turned to for my cat but unfortunately it is part of that pack of vets attached only to the money that is not worth paying them they study a lot in vain I found it very bad a lot of money very little professionalism and humanity.
No. 1.

Unfortunately, I must point out that, despite being a client and often having good experiences, this morning, after waiting an hour and twenty minutes, I had to leave because my brachycephalic dog, whom I brought for dermatitis, was in danger of collapsing from the stress and heat. I didn't get anything done, I wasted two hours, and no one from the facility contacted me.

So... We're in the realm of personal assessments, so please take that into account.
We arrived with our beloved dog, who was in very critical condition due to a respiratory crisis caused by ongoing pneumonia.
Upon immediate admission, the dog underwent immediate rehabilitation, something that the "usual" vet and another emergency clinic had been unable to provide. After the usual, long wait, we had a thorough examination, blood tests, and x-rays. Pneumonia was diagnosed, treatment was prescribed, and the dog was given a course of treatment.
Expected costs.
Highly recommended for anyone with an emergency, and I think I'll also use them for my pets' regular checkups, if I can.
Doctors Marco and Lorenzo are excellent. Thank you for everything.
We are happy to know that our efforts are appreciated and that you had a positive experience with us.

On Monday, August 3rd, around 4:30 a.m., a friend and I brought my cat in after he'd vomited twice in quick succession, the last time containing blood. That same day, early in the morning, he was scheduled to see his veterinarian (luckily, there are still doctors with a capital D). We'd already spoken to him on Saturday and had agreed to update him and intervene sooner if he continued. Upon arriving (and visibly agitated), I was greeted by a pigtailed "doctor" and what I presumed was a nurse, both of whom were anything but friendly. The aforementioned doctor's demeanor was more like someone whose doorbell had just been rung at 4 a.m. than the doorbell of a VETERINARY EMERGENCY ROOM. Annoyed and unwilling to listen, after looking at his watch and opening the door, he didn't even ask me to explain the situation properly, much less ask for clarification. I simply felt attacked and judged. Then, a few seconds later, while we were standing in the waiting room (quite shocked and incredulous at his attitude), he reminded me, in an extremely rude manner, that there were several emergencies at that moment (I remember the nurse/other doctor was standing there, watching and glaring... so the emergencies were obviously waiting) and that he would be off at 8, so there would be a wait. At which point, shocked and very angry, I pointed out, with far too much politeness, that this didn't seem appropriate for an emergency room, for a DOCTOR, and that, if that were the tone and the premise, since I needed to have him examined, I would leave. I was told to go elsewhere, rudely dismissed, and wished me a good evening. Fortunately, my cat was seen by another clinic and, subsequently, by his veterinarian, people who listened and provided treatment, which he is still undergoing. However, if things had gone differently and it had been something more serious, these people would have been jointly responsible. They didn't have me explain things properly, they didn't ask me questions, they didn't have a clear picture of the situation, and, consequently, they had no basis for deeming the situation serious or less serious than the others. But even if they had asked me for more information, if the situation had actually not been serious and there were truly other, more serious emergencies that took priority (as they should), there are proper ways and manners to communicate anything, and these were not the least bit. Regarding this horrifying experience, do I need to say anything else? I don't think so. Only one thing: SHAME ON YOU.
At the reception the staff is not trained to welcome customers
We are happy to know that our efforts are appreciated and that you had a positive experience with us.

No... good, but unfortunately they're a bit rushed... there are some very good doctors... but some (very young) are not very empathetic and explain in "medical jargon"... an approach not very appropriate to stressful situations... (I emphasize that my impression was an observer, I was accompanying a friend). The sonographer was very knowledgeable and welcoming.
Thank you for your positive feedback! Pet welfare and owner satisfaction are our top priorities.
They couldn't help me with an exotic parrot

Terrible experience: lack of professionalism and zero empathy
Unfortunately, I can only confirm the feeling that in this facility, animals are treated merely as numbers and a profit opportunity, rather than as patients to be treated with respect.
After having my dog ​​undergo an endless series of extremely expensive procedures and tests, I would have expected a completely different level of expertise and attention. It's unacceptable that, despite the huge expense and constant testing (driven, in my opinion, solely by the desire to generate as much revenue as possible), the clinic wasn't even able to determine the dog's blood type, a crucial piece of information for his safety. Furthermore, there was a complete lack of thoroughness in reading and cross-referencing the results of routine tests. When we went beyond routine diagnoses and delved into more complex situations, their response was always the same: they simply said the dog was "fine," and then immediately suggested another series of completely useless tests instead of providing us with concrete answers.
To top off this unpleasant experience, I encountered a lack of customer service: after a phone call for clarification, I received rude, to say the least, responses that ended with the phone being slammed down in my face.
The health and lives of our dogs require care, compassion, and expertise, all of which were completely lacking here. I strongly advise against this facility to anyone looking for a reliable, caring service with even a modicum of empathy for their pets.
Terrible hospital where they only think about profit without considering the animals' best interests. If you love your animals, avoid them.

From a medical and nursing perspective, I can only thank you. I must especially praise Dr. Maisto and her nurse for the sensitivity and competence with which they handled the euthanasia of my son's little kitten.
I must, however, highlight the terrible management of the administrative staff when it came time to settle the bill. The first employee disputed the amount I had paid the night before, claiming that I had left 300 euros when in reality I had paid 600. Luckily, I had the receipt. Despite this, still unsure, she asked for the assistance of another colleague. Frankly, I felt embarrassed!
Once the formalities were completed and the bills settled, we left, and while we were in the parking lot, I heard my last name being called out loud in front of everyone. A second employee, whom I had initially asked how to make the payment, called me, as I said, from a distance, telling me that I had to settle the bill. If I felt embarrassed with the first employee, with the second I felt truly ashamed!! To avoid arguments about the procedures, and given our emotional state over the kitten's euthanasia, we simply pointed out that we had already paid for it... I wasn't running away!
I reiterate, however, that I am completely satisfied with the care provided to the little kitten. The care center is excellent. Thanks also to the doctor who admitted her the night before in the emergency room.
Thank you so much.

The entire staff is extremely knowledgeable and friendly.
Dog and Cat provided us with every type of information we asked for.
Avoid this place. Endless waits with no news. Four hours of waiting without a doctor even bothering to let you know. Since they moved, the service has significantly deteriorated—a shame.
We are happy to know that our efforts are appreciated and that you had a positive experience with us.

Terrible experience. My dog ​​died.
We took the dog to the ER at 6:00 AM, which was the closest emergency room to our home. The dog was in terrible pain but still conscious. The vets there... not only showed no empathy, they also seemed unwilling to touch the dog. They left him alone in the room without running the tests they'd initially advised. The dog remained in the room for hours and hours while he fought for his life.
The dog that pooped and peed on his body wasn't cleaned or even looked at. My mother asked for another rug, and it took them 20 minutes to bring that too.
When we decided to take the dog, who had lost precious hours of his life, to another vet, the only thing they said was, "You have to pay before you leave." That's 170 for doing nothing but laying the dog down.
People who don't care about animal welfare and only care about money. Shame on you.
Positive experience. Attentive, professional, and courteous.
Thank you for your positive feedback! Pet welfare and owner satisfaction are our top priorities.
Qualified staff, excellent welcome... EXCELLENCE
Thank you for sharing your experience and for your trust in us! We work passionately to ensure quality care and attention for all the pets who trust us.

Bad experience. I brought my cat in on Friday at 8:15 PM, and after a 3-hour wait, they finally saw her. The cat is elderly and hadn't eaten for 2 days. I asked for fluids, but nothing happened. They did an X-ray and an ultrasound. It all cost €209, and I was supposed to bring her back the next day. I went to another clinic, where they admitted her immediately and put her on fluids! They also told me the X-ray was useless. Really awful!

We need more humanity. A person brings in a dying animal and they charge you 300 euros. I'm not saying don't pay, but beyond the pain, these are figures that don't inspire compassion. The Lord knows we are all children of God. 🔥💙🙏 …

A very negative experience. A friend of mine brought her dog to this clinic because he was very ill. Instead of offering further tests or attempting a life-saving operation, euthanasia was almost immediately recommended.

Unconvinced, we took the dog to another veterinary facility, where he underwent emergency surgery. He is currently hospitalized and in critical condition, but he is alive and receiving all necessary care.

We understand that, in some extreme cases, euthanasia may be an option to avoid unnecessary suffering. However, we believe that a veterinarian's first duty is to carefully evaluate all treatment options and attempt to save the animal when there is still a real chance. In our case, fortunately, we sought a second opinion.

Terrible experience.
Not to mention the hospital stay costs: €300 a night puts you in a position where you have to give up. For everything, they show you the quotes first, then the problem. The dog was operated on and cared for from June 30th to July 9th, and we're looking at a quote of €5,100.00, reaching the point of requesting voluntary discharge, which is also a problem because they try to stall for other days that are convenient for them. There's no way to communicate with a doctor; it's all a buck-passing exercise.

This morning we used the emergency room service at this excellent facility.
Unfortunately, there was nothing that could be done for our cat Oneira due to complications that arose.
I must say, I have no words for the healthcare staff and for Dr. Nicola CASADIO, professional and, above all, humane care. I have no words to describe the TOTAL approach they had with the patient and, ultimately, with us.
Money donations should pour in for these types of facilities, especially this one, which is managed with a vocational focus on animals.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart, and may God BLESS every moment of your work...
Beautiful structure, qualified staff

This morning, July 8, 2026, at 5:30 a.m., I went to the emergency room to take my 3-year-old Labrador because he's had diarrhea and blood for days. I explained the problem, explaining what I was worried about (he'd ingested something he shouldn't have), and they told me it was 5 a.m., which was early. They annoyed me, dismissing me by saying, "It must be chronic," without even examining him, standing in the hallway with the door propped open with their hand.
It's a shame I didn't ask the doctor's name, but it's easy to find out who was on duty this morning.
I was truly speechless!!!
Extremely expensive

Excellent! A new, well-organized and welcoming environment. Plenty of space in the reception area and comfortable waiting areas. Friendly staff and kind, helpful doctors.
I've known this hospital for years and have always had a great experience. Now that they've moved to this new facility, it's even better. Excellence!
🔝🐕👍

They saved the life of my elderly Jak, without any expectations, they are all very good, human, you can see in them the dedication to the work they have chosen, I also had to end up in the emergency room where there are super and well-prepared doctors, what can I say, I have been their satellite customer for more than 20 years, but they never disappoint me.
Thank you for sharing your experience and for your trust in us! We work passionately to ensure quality care and attention for all the pets who trust us.
Competence and professionalism. The entire staff is excellent. You saved our dog, and I will be forever grateful! I'm giving it 4 stars because of the price, which is unfortunately too high.
Modern and well-equipped hospital. I went back to the same doctor as last year because she was very good and very clear in her explanations. The receptionists were also very quick and kind.
Organized and competent. Waits can be very long if you haven't booked.

I'm giving it one star because it wouldn't get you half a star!! If it were up to them, I would have lost my two-and-a-half-year-old dog to immunological meningoencephalitis. After undergoing I don't know how many tests, including an MRI with contrast and a cervical spinal fluid sampling, they said there was nothing neurological.
I took the tests they performed to another clinic (luckily for me!) and got the diagnosis!
I only wasted precious time due to their incompetence!!! In these cases, a timely diagnosis is crucial!
Thank you for your review! Our team works hard every day to provide the best service possible.
We're so happy to read your review! Our team works passionately to offer the best for every pet. Thank you for sharing your experience!
Exorbitant prices 1,200 euros to put stitches my vet 200 euros. Luckily I took it away

I'm sure there are excellent veterinarians working with the facility, but unfortunately, we were not treated well. We arrived in the evening because the cat had been sick since the afternoon. He was vomiting and very listless, not eating or drinking—very unusual symptoms for him. The doctor greeted us by saying, "Did you come because the cat was vomiting?" I think it's pretty obvious that if someone shows up at the emergency room at night, it's because they think the situation is serious enough; otherwise, they'd happily stay in bed and sleep 😅. Anyway, they did tests and an X-ray and told us the cat was fine, nothing wrong with him, adding, "If he continues to feel sick, do an abdominal ultrasound."

Spoiler: the next day the cat underwent emergency surgery (obviously at another clinic) because he had intestinal intussusception and they had to remove a piece of intestine that had died. I wonder how it's possible to go from "he's fine" to an emergency operation. Furthermore, the reason he underwent surgery was explained to us as being VERY common in Maine Coons, so why did the other vet immediately notice it and not you? How come they immediately saw from the tests that something was wrong and you didn't? It will remain a mystery. We are human, we all make mistakes, but welcoming a patient and saying, "Hey, you came because the cat is vomiting," making a mistake, even a huge one, in the diagnosis makes everything unpleasant.

Really disappointing... 😕 The call center staff is practically nonexistent, they answer randomly... and if you're lucky and manage to speak to an operator, they're arrogant and even hang up on you. 😳
For a prescription for parasite control, 5 days... and they still haven't sent it to me. HORRIBLE
Obviously, I'll look elsewhere.
We're so happy to read your review! Our team works passionately to offer the best for every pet. Thank you for sharing your experience!

To extract hundreds of euros more, they offer pet owners unnecessary procedures, as they are often too old to care for them. They also exploit the emotional state of patients, who would do anything for their four-legged friends. The result? Death of your four-legged friend! What's worse, they boast a NON-EXISTENT 24-HOUR CENTRE, especially during the NIGHT. Hospitalized pets are not cared for. Yet, this service is paid dearly. DO NOT LEAVE THEM THERE ALONE! Especially during the night!!!!!
My experience was positive. Special praise goes to Dr. Serena Sessa, who was empathetic, compassionate, and thorough in her explanations.
I bring my dog ​​to the clinic with various problems related to her advanced age, and I've always had a great experience. Plus, my favorite vet, Dr. Sanna, works there. 🐶🐶 …
Very kind staff, we felt welcomed and listened to about a problem with our dachshund.

One star for the 4-hour wait to prepare my dog ​​for sedation and then the ultrasound. We arrived at 11:00 AM, and they let us in at 2:30 PM, repeatedly asking everyone to come in before us. I understand we had to wait for the procedures, but 4.5 hours seems excessive without even getting a definitive answer. In the end, when we got angry and were about to leave, they let us in. I repeat, my rating is for the wait; the vets were professional with my dog, even though they have a very complicated dog.
Excellent organization, kind and efficient staff. I found the doctor who treated my French bulldog, Luna, to be very competent and kind.
As always, efficiency, courtesy and availability from Dr. Radighieri

I'd like to share a thought...my dog ​​is no longer with us today...I hope that one day things will improve on this issue: it doesn't concern the admission of animals that can be treated with little effort...but it concerns animals that enter a serious state of health. I wish we could be more direct towards people and not always push them to do test after test, knowing that there's nothing more that can be done. It's anguish, both for the owner and for the animal. I hope there's more sensitivity towards the people who choose you to help them with their life's joys, and more patience from the receptionists. They are delicate roles.
We should be more patient, but I understand that a person has to feel it from within. We are not numbers, or at least I still believe in humanity. I send a hug to all the people who suffer for the health of their greatest joys, ❤️ it's a way to share with you readers... a thought of mine.
State-of-the-art, clean, functional clinic, excellent staff
Highly recommended
Second time that i've been here the staff very profecional  and caring

3 hours in the waiting room, FORTY MINUTES TO CHANGE SHIFT, FORTY.
Then of course there were the emergencies and bye bye, my dears, not even triage, nothing.
Thank you for your review! Our team works hard every day to provide the best service possible.
Your kind words truly make us happy! Our team works hard every day to provide attentive and professional service. Knowing that you appreciate our work is the best reward. Thank you for your trust!
We are happy to know that our efforts are appreciated and that you had a positive experience with us.
Thank you for your review! Our team works hard every day to provide the best service possible.
We're so happy to read your review! Our team works passionately to offer the best for every pet. Thank you for sharing your experience!

The hospital is called Gregorio VII because it was actually at the end of Via Gregorio VII (Piazza Villa Carpegna), in a basement easily accessible by both metro and car, with two directly integrated garages. Now they've built a new facility accessible only by car, but via improbable and extremely busy roads. The facility looks nice, but efficiency hasn't improved; quite the opposite. After a certain hour, the clinic closes, and the emergency room is cramped, smaller, and more poorly furnished than before. They have such a long line for emergencies that a single foxtail causes a four-hour wait. The wait before (it's understandable), during (I have a complaint about the anesthesia dosages—my dog ​​was knocked out for a night, and in the past, the anesthesia for an operation wore off in half an hour), and after... to pay (intolerable). The staff is nice but understaffed and employed outside of their roles (the doctors also do accounting), and inevitably (against their will) forced to be inefficient. My dachshund woke up paralyzed this morning, February 14, at 3:30 a.m. Since, unfortunately, we'd already had the same experience, we rushed her to the Gregorio VII clinic. Once we arrived at the emergency room, we were mistreated by the doctor on call, who barely deigned to look at her, telling us we had to wait for the neurologists who would arrive at 10 a.m. (This was at 5:30 a.m., after a 120 km drive in a hurry to get her operated on as quickly as possible, because even the walls know that in these cases, the sooner the intervention, the better the chances of a better outcome). We asked if we could leave her so she could get some painkillers, tests, or a CT scan or MRI, but they said no and that she would only be seen when the neurologists arrived, which was a good five hours later. What can we say about the humanity and professionalism underfoot, at least as far as the emergency room doctors are concerned. I'd like to point out that our other dachshund, with the same problem, underwent surgery at this clinic but was fortunate enough to be taken in directly by the neurology team, which was excellent. Unfortunately, however, the professional standards aren't the same across all departments, it seems. The emergency room, and I say this as a doctor, should be able to handle emergencies and stabilize them before a specialist arrives. So, what's the point of your 24-hour emergency room?
We finally took her to the CVRS Policlinico Roma Sud clinic, another center of excellence in veterinary neurology, where they welcomed us with open arms and immediately performed the necessary tests for a neurological evaluation. So if it's helpful to someone with a nighttime emergency like this, I highly recommend this other clinic.
